thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stock Futures Point Slightly Higher As Nasdaq Attempts To End 3-day Skid

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stock Futures Point Slightly Higher As Nasdaq Attempts To End 3-day Skid
text:
By Victor Reklaitis, MarketWatch , Ryan Vlastelica
With one day left in July, the Dow is up 4.3% for the month
U.S. stock-index futures pointed to a modestly higher open on Tuesday, suggesting some stabilization in stocks following a stretch of losses that took the Nasdaq to its lowest level in weeks.
What are the main benchmarks doing?
Dow Jones Industrial Average futures rose 31 points, or 0.1%, to 25,317, while S&P 500 futures added 7.3 points, or 0.3%, to 2,810. Nasdaq-100 futures added 21 points, or 0.3%, to 7,222.
On Monday, the Dow , S&P and Nasdaq Composite all slumped (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-stock-futures-dip-putting-sp-500-on-pace-for-3rd-down-session-in-a-row-2018-07-30), leaving the Nasdaq down by 3.8% over the past three sessions. Both the S&P and the Nasdaq have dropped for three straight trading days, while the Dow has dropped for two.
With one session left in July, the Dow is up 4.3% for the month, while the S&P and Nasdaq have tacked on 3.1% and 1.6%, respectively.
What's driving markets?
Investors continued to digest an onslaught of quarterly earnings reports. While the season has generally come in well ahead of expectations, there were some high-profile misses, including from Silicon Valley juggernauts Facebook Inc (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/facebook-stock-crushed-after-revenue-user-growth-miss-2018-07-25). (FB)and Twitter Inc (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/twitter-user-numbers-slip-as-it-purges-fake-accounts-2018-07-27-7103732).(TWTR). Both stocks have tumbled in recent sessions, and the pressure they put on technology stocks have weighed on the broader market.
Not only are tech stocks among the largest in the market, but they have also been among the biggest gainers in 2018, meaning broader indexes could be vulnerable in the event they continue to slide.
Tech will remain in focus throughout the session, as investors await quarterly results from Apple Inc.(AAPL) (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-earnings-most-boring-quarter-of-the-year-still-holds-some-intrigue-2018-07-27), which will be released after the market closes (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-earnings-most-boring-quarter-of-the-year-still-holds-some-intrigue-2018-07-27).
What are strategists saying?
"Tech investors have their eyes on Apple today," said Naeem Aslam, chief market analyst at ThinkMarkets, in a note. He said the iPhone maker's earnings "may save" the Nasdaq.
Which economic reports are on tap?
June readings on personal incomes, consumer spending and core inflation are due at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time, and a release on second-quarter employment costs is also expected at that time.
At 9 a.m. Eastern, investors are slated to get a May report on home prices. A July release on business conditions in the Chicago area is scheduled to hit at 9:45 a.m. Eastern, followed by a May figure for consumer confidence at 10 a.m. Eastern.
Check out:MarketWatch's Economic Calendar (http://www.marketwatch.com/economy-politics/calendars/economic)
The Federal Reserve's policy makers are due to start a two-day meeting. They are expected to signal on Wednesday that more interest-rate hikes are coming (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/fed-to-send-clear-message-that-more-rate-hikes-are-coming-2018-07-27), but not to raise rates at this month's meeting.
In other central bank news, the Bank of Japan bucked market expectations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/bank-of-japan-surprises-by-keeping-its-ultra-easy-monetary-policy-in-place-2018-07-31) and kept its ultra-easy monetary policy, sending the dollar up against the yen .
Which stocks are in focus?
Pfizer Inc.(PFE) reported adjusted second-quarter earnings that beat expectations, along with revenue that was ahead of forecasts (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/pfizer-tops-estimates-for-the-second-quarter-and-raises-profit-guidance-2018-07-31). Shares of the Dow component were little changed before the bell.
Procter & Gamble Co.(PG) reported adjusted fourth-quarter earnings that beat expectations but revenue that was slightly below consensus forecasts. The consumer-products giant also gave a soft outlook for its 2019 fiscal year (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/pg-shares-slip-after-soft-fiscal-2019-guidance-2018-07-31), sending shares down 2.1% in premarket trading.
Archer Daniels Midland Co.(ADM) reported adjusted second-quarter earnings and revenue that both came in sharply ahead of expectations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/archer-daniels-shares-pop-2-premarket-after-earnings-blow-past-estimates-2018-07-31). The stock jumped 4% in premarket trading.
Cummins Inc. (CMI) reported second-quarter earnings that missed expectations, but revenue that was ahead of forecasts (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/cummins-tops-revenue-estimates-sending-stock-up-28-premarket-2018-07-31). Shares rose 2.8% before the bell.
BP PLC (BP.LN) reported a jump in its second-quarter earnings, supported by higher oil prices (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/bp-profit-shoots-up-boosted-by-higher-oil-prices-2018-07-31). U.S.-listed shares gained 1.6% in premarket trading.
Lumber Liquidators Holdings Inc.(LL) sank 9.8% in premarket trading after it reported a surprise second-quarter loss, though revenue was ahead of expectations (http://www.marketwatch.com/discover).
Charter Communications Inc.(CHTR) reported second-quarter earnings that beat expectations.
Qualcomm Inc. (QCOM) launched a tender offer to repurchase up to $10 billion in stock (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/qualcomm-stock-gains-after-company-details-10-billion-buyback-plan-2018-07-31). Shares rose 2.7% in premarket trading.
Shopify Inc. (SHOP) jumped 1.7% in premarket trading after it reported second-quarter earnings that beat expectations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/shopify-shares-rise-after-revenue-beat-2018-07-31).
Steve Madden Ltd. (SHOO) reported adjusted second-quarter earnings that beat expectations, along with revenue that topped consensus analyst forecasts (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/steve-madden-beats-earnings-and-revenue-estimates-2018-07-31).
Shire PLC (SHPG) reported a sharp increase in its second-quarter earnings, supported by booking lower costs and higher sales (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/shire-profit-soars-as-sales-rise-backs-guidance-2018-07-31).
What are other markets doing?
Oil futures and gold futures were falling, while the dollar index was little changed. European stocks (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-stocks-search-for-firm-direction-as-earnings-roll-in-with-inflation-data-in-focus-2018-07-31)traded mixed, after Asia finished mixed (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-mixed-as-investors-wait-on-bank-of-japan-announcement-2018-07-30).
